t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup: an asymmetric bento grid on a deep navy background. Top-left, a large light-weight sans headline and short intro on the navy. A tall central tile split by a soft wavy edge into navy and warm limestone holds a photo-real render of clear glass cubes in a lattice with splashing water, glowing cyan dot callouts and a small caption. Smaller white and limestone tiles around it show <CONTENT> as oversized monospace figures with units, small uppercase labels, monospace citations, plus-sign corner marks, a faint chemical-structure watermark and one grayscale micrograph strip. One steel-blue accent figure. Precise, calm, scientific.
signature_idea: Each limit is a tile whose oversized mono number is the headline, gathered around one tall tile where a glass lattice dissolves into water.
strengths: limit numbers are instantly scannable and given their own weight
mono figures and citation footers fit a spec-reading audience
palette (navy, limestone, white, one steel-blue) is close to the brand book
bento gives a strong but orderly rhythm
standard references are placed consistently on each tile
weaknesses: TOC tile is duplicated, wasting space and confusing
glass-cube render is abstract and decorative; its caption claims a meaning it does not show
microbe micrograph is a stock-science cliché and slightly unsettling
rounded tile corners break the square-corner rule
circuit icon on conductivity tile is generic tech iconography
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone with one steel-blue accent, light headline and mono figures are on-brand and calm, but rounded tiles, a decorative glass render and stock micrograph dilute the precise line-drawing language.
